title: Route-and-invoice app for small pool service companies
subtitle: Quick stress-test of a cheaper, simpler Skimmer alternative for solo and small pool routes, from App Store reviews and vendor pricing pages.

founder.channel: online; cousin runs a 2-truck pool route and can make intros

verdict.summary: The pain is real: six different Skimmer reviewers describe repeated price hikes, and another app's owner-operator with 20 stops saw his bill go from $65 to $115. But "cheaper" is already for sale (Paythepoolman at $50 + $15 per tech, QuoteIQ from $29.99) and Skimmer's own $1-per-pool tier is cheap for a small route, so a price wedge alone is thin. Pivot the angle to an offline-first, fast route log with a written price lock for owner-operators, and test it through your cousin's network before building. Customer voice comes from App Store reviews only (Reddit and the review sites blocked this network), so treat it as directional.

opportunities.name: Cheaper, simpler Skimmer for small pool routes
opportunities.one_liner: Route, service log and invoicing at a lower, predictable price for solo and 1-3 truck pool companies.
opportunities.why: Pain 6: price hikes and reliability complaints repeat across 7+ different App Store reviewers on three apps (e1-e9, e10-e14, e25, e26), but it is one source type and Skimmer still holds 4.62 stars on 3,716 ratings, with loyal fans (e23, e24). Willingness to pay 7: they already pay $49 to $147+ a month and complain about the amount, not about paying (e3, e8, e9, o1-o5). Competition gap 3: per-tech pricing from Paythepoolman and QuoteIQ already undercuts per-pool billing for small routes (o3, o6), Skimmer's own $1 tier is cheap at small scale (o1), and at least nine new pool-route apps are already in the App Store (o8-o11). Founder fit 7: React Native + Node is exactly the stack, $2k covers it, but offline sync, payments and accounting integration at 15 hours a week is months, not weeks. Reachability 5: the cousin's network is a real warm channel, but this run could not verify any public community (Reddit blocked), and App Store reviewers can't be contacted. Build cost 5: a few months of work for offline sync, invoicing and payments.

gap.statement: Owner-operators with a small pool route can't get a route-and-invoice app that stays fast and stays the same price, because every option keeps adding features, repricing per pool or per tech, and slowing down in the field.

pains.summary: Per-pool rates doubled, legacy features repriced, repeated increase notices.

pains.theme: Slow, crashing, loses sync in the field
pains.summary: Crashes, scrambled routes, no offline mode on bad signal.

pains.theme: Features nobody asked for, then a higher bill
pains.summary: Bloat slows the app; old features gated behind new tiers.
Weeks to hear back; months of calls about the same issue.
Payment fees above QuickBooks; wants invoicing from the app.

weaknesses: General field-service, not pool-specific (vendor claims only)

critic.risk: Cheaper alternatives already exist: Paythepoolman ($50 + $15/tech), QuoteIQ (from $29.99), and at least nine new pool-route apps in the App Store with almost no ratings.
Skimmer's own Getting Started tier is $1 per pool, so a solo with a small route already pays little; the price wedge is thin.
Switching cost: owners have years of customer and service data in Skimmer (one reviewer says so).
critic.rebuttal: Only one reviewer raised it (e22); free CSV import and a done-for-you migration address it directly.
They pay today and complain about the amount, not about paying (e3, e8, e9).
One search found no shutdowns, only consolidation (Fluidra bought Pooltrackr). The category is being bought, not abandoned.

critic.risk: Skimmer can cut small-route prices whenever it wants.

win_plan.positioning: The pool route app for owner-operators that works with no signal and never changes price.

switching_triggers.move: Written lifetime price lock plus free import, offered through warm intros the week notices go out

switching_triggers.trigger: A bad day in the field from crashes or lost sync
switching_triggers.move: Offline-first route log demo on the owner's own route

offers: Written price lock for as long as you stay

trust: Public price with a written no-increase promise
stop_doing: Per-pool metering that grows with every customer
Moving old features behind new tiers (e17)

pricing.recommendation: Flat $29 to $39/mo per company up to ~75 pools, price-locked; test the number in interviews
pricing.competitor_range: $1 to $2 per pool (Skimmer, PoolDial), $15 to $65 per tech, $29.99+ per user
pricing.rationale: Must at least match QuoteIQ and Paythepoolman on price, so price is a floor, not the wedge; the lock and the offline reliability are the pitch.

validation.experiment: Ten 20-minute calls with owner-operators via your cousin, showing a clickable offline route-log prototype and a price-lock offer.
validation.pass_bar: 5 of 10 agree to pre-pay the first month or join a paid pilot
steps: Day 1: ask your cousin for 10 intros to solo or 1-3 truck owners
Day 2-3: build a clickable prototype of the offline route log and invoice
Day 4-6: run the calls; ask what they pay now, last price notice, and what broke last week
Day 7: count pre-pay commitments against the pass bar

kill_criteria: Fewer than 3 of 10 owners will pre-pay
Most owners say Skimmer's $1 tier or Paythepoolman is fine for them
Nobody names a reliability or offline problem unprompted
